description:
FILED s540e (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-15).  The s540e brief (member 1, #4989) asked that the Clone shim use the deep-copy primitive too.  NOT DONE in s540e: the primitive s540e built is dclone's (it DECLINES on every kind the Storable format path must handle, and canonicalises scalars as a round trip through the format does), and lib/Clone.pm's walk differs from it in five places -- holes become undef with the array's length kept (`@$copy = map {...} @$ref`), CODE / GLOB / IO / FORMAT / Regexp referents are SHARED, scalars keep their exact faces (a double stays a double; a dualvar stays dual), clone($ref, $depth) stops at a depth, a tied container is read through FETCH.  Converting it changes HOW Clone copies and needs its own differential probe against Clone.xs 0.47 (installed on this box).

Design: a policy argument to builtin::deep_copy (or a sibling name sharing the walk) -- :share-special, :exact-scalars, :holes-undef, a depth bound -- the walk struct carries it; the decline answer stays for tied / magic / dual so the Perl walk remains the fallback.  Gain: s540b measured Clone::clone of a small nested hash at 3,000 copies in 0.084 s whole run (perl dclone 0.013 s); dclone through deep_copy is ~1.2 us a call on the s540e tree.

BAR: probe vs Clone.xs (the #3826 guard program + holes, shared CODE, a depth limit, a dualvar, a tied hash); Pl/t guard rows; the gain measured.
subject: OPEN (s540e): the Clone shim still walks in Perl -- route it through builtin::deep_copy (rule 11: one copier) with Clone's own policy (CODE / GLOB / IO / FORMAT / Regexp SHARED, not declined; scalar faces copied exactly, not canonical; holes read as undef and the length kept; the depth argument; a tied container read through), measured and differentially probed against Clone.xs 0.47
